title: Scan only the request's own text at admission, not named files
summary: The admission boundary-word scan (`scan_request_input` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs) also scans every file a request names, so naming BRIEF.md refuses the request. Change it to scan only the request text. Named files are still scanned when a candidate changes them, as today. The audience is the owner, who names BRIEF.md in requests.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust code and tests.
Tests added or updated; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test must pass.
Tests exercise admission of a request naming a file with a boundary word, and refusal of a request with one in its own text.
Fixes the scan scope at its source in scan_request_input, not just for BRIEF.md.
One focused change to the scan plus its tests and the changelog.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
A criterion checks that a request naming the brief file is admitted.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. `scan_request_input` (line ~2030) scans the request text, then each file found by `request_text_touches`. `refuse_banned_input` calls it from the two ask entry points (lines ~715 and ~740). I also read crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (test near line 2440-2484, which asserts that a dirty named file is refused, and calls `scan_request_input` directly) and crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs. admission.rs holds no boundary scan. It is named in the request, but the scan lives in reading.rs.
No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test do not apply.
The existing run/mod.rs test expects a named dirty file to be refused at admission. It must be updated to the new behavior: the named file is admitted, the request's own banned word is still refused.
The scan of files a candidate changes (the xtask policy test and the check on a candidate's changed files) stays untouched. `check_boundary_and_repo_files` still scans reading text.

The `scan_request_input` signature may stay the same or drop its git parameters; the producer decides. It keeps the request-text findings and the `InputFinding` type. Any other caller, such as the one in run/mod.rs, is updated.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-core shows that a request naming an existing file with a boundary word (such as BRIEF.md or a docs file) but whose own text has none is admitted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A test shows that a request whose own text holds a boundary word is still refused with a 'not admitted' error naming source `request`. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

`scan_request_input` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs no longer reads named files at admission, and its doc comment and the `refuse_banned_input` message describe request-only scanning. The old test in run/mod.rs that expected a named dirty file to be refused is replaced.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying admission scans only the request's own text, not the files it names, and says why: the owner's brief legitimately uses boundary words.
The change refuses fewer readings, not more; no new refusal rule is added. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.

out_of_scope: Changing the boundary word lists or `boundary_scan` in athena-context.
Changing the scan of files a candidate changes (xtask policy test, verification).
Editing BRIEF.md or any file under records/.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
departures: The named file admission.rs holds no scan; the real code is in reading.rs and run/mod.rs, so the request's file list is incomplete. That slightly raises the risk the user questions the reading.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: requests that name BRIEF.md are refused for words they do not contain, which forces rejected attempts and rewording.
hard_reason: Changes a refusal rule: the admission gate that refuses requests holding boundary words, so a mistake could let banned words through or keep refusing valid requests.
